setup: A non-production account under accounts/<domain>/ with profile.json (an admin key). Replace <domain> with it. Nothing else is needed: each eval creates its own script and endpoint, named with a test prefix.

evals.prompt: Create an endpoint on <domain> that receives a JSON with an email and returns whether a contact with that email exists. Only signed-in users should be able to call it.
evals.expected_output: A handler script laid out by hand and published with ./prolibu script dev, an authenticated POST endpoint created through scripts/endpoint.js after a yes, and a test call with and without a token.
expectations: Writes accounts/<domain>/scripts/<prefix>/index.js with Events.on('EndpointRequest') and Events.init() as the last statement, without running ./prolibu script create
Uses its own API key from the script's variables (ProlibuApi) to read contacts, not the caller's token
Runs endpoint.js preview, shows the URL with the lowercase verb, waits for a yes, then apply --confirmed
Calls it with endpoint.js call both with a token (200, reads output) and with --no-auth (401)

evals.prompt: Necesito una URL para recibir los webhooks de pago de nuestro proveedor. Firman el cuerpo con HMAC-SHA256 en hex en el header X-Signature, con un secreto que nos dieron.
evals.expected_output: Answered in Spanish: a public POST endpoint whose script verifies the HMAC with lib/utils/hmacSha256.js and timingSafeEqual, with the secret in the script's variables and the caveat about the raw body.
expectations: Says HMAC verification is possible in a script with lib/utils/hmacSha256.js (does not claim it is impossible)
Explains the script only gets the parsed body, so the signature matches only if the provider sends compact JSON (or text/plain), and asks or checks how the provider serializes
Creates the endpoint with authentication.enabled false and warns the sender must not send an Authorization header
Keeps the secret out of the code: script variables set in the app with config.json without a variables key, or in config.json not committed
A bad signature returns output { ok: false } instead of throwing

evals.prompt: Our endpoint answers 400 'requestUser is not defined' when our partner calls it, but it works when I test it from the app.
evals.expected_output: Explains requestUser only exists for authenticated calls and the partner calls anonymously; fixes the script with a typeof guard.
expectations: Identifies that requestUser is only defined when the call carries a valid token
Fix uses typeof requestUser === 'undefined' (or equivalent) instead of reading it directly
Republishes the script with ./prolibu script dev/prod after a yes and re-tests with endpoint.js call --no-auth

evals.prompt: Make the sync endpoint accept both GET to read and POST to write, with two endpoints called 'sync'.
evals.expected_output: Explains routeName is unique across methods and that any verb reaches the same endpoint; proposes two route names or one handler that branches on a body field.
expectations: Says a second endpoint with the same routeName is rejected
Says the script cannot see which HTTP verb was used
Proposes distinct route names (for example sync-pull and sync-push) or one route that reads an action from the body or query
